In the figure, the vertical line segment from the midpoint of the bottom side to the highest point of the lower semicircle is labeled 1, indicating that the semicircle radius is 1. Reasoning: Let the center of the square be the origin, and the side length be s, then the centers of the four semicircles are respectively (0, s/2), (s/2, 0), (0, -s/2), (-s/2, 0). The distance between the centers of two adjacent semicircles is sqrt((s/2)^2 + (s/2)^2) = s/sqrt(2). Since the adjacent unit semicircles in the figure are tangent, the distance between centers equals 1 + 1 = 2, so s/sqrt(2) = 2, obtaining s = 2sqrt(2). The center of the central circle is at the center of the square, and its distance to the center of any semicircle is s/2 = sqrt(2). The central circle is externally tangent to the semicircular arc with radius 1, therefore sqrt(2) = 1 + r, so r = sqrt(2) - 1.
